body:
If you read last week's blog, you might recall that I had a "Cautious" outlook for the market this week, as I believed the jump in oil prices and U.S./Iran re-escalation was not being fully discounted by investors. At the time of this writing (1:34 p.m. ET) all the majors are on track to be down modestly on the week, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq  Composite being the worst performer (-1.4%). The exchange of attacks between the U.S. and Iran continued this week and oil prices continued to climb [...] from 71.14%, the CCMP (blue line) fell to 43.54% vs. 46.53%, and the RUT (red line) pulled back to 63.36% versus 67.86% (all week-over-week). [...] Thursday (July 30): Continuing Claims, EIA Natural Gas Inventories, Q2 GDP – Advanced Reading, Initial Claims, PCE Prices, Personal Income, Personal Spending

## US stocks and economy

Our perspective on what's driving U.S. equity markets

Market Snapshot | February 2023

We believe rising oil prices and higher yields represent an emerging risk that could influence the Fed’s policy path in the months ahead and contribute to greater market volatility as we head into the seasonally softer August and September period. However, underlying economic and corporate fundamentals remain constructive, in our view, supporting a cautiously optimistic outlook for the back half of the year. [...] Against this backdrop, we remain neutral duration relative to the benchmark. However, we are raising our expected range for where the 10-year Treasury may trade over the remainder of the year to 4.5%–5.0% (from 4.0%–4.5%), reflecting both renewed energy-driven inflation pressures from the U.S.–Iran conflict and the Fed’s heightened sensitivity to upside inflation surprises.

### AI narratives remain in the driver's seat for stocks [...] On the equity side, we think higher rates might start pressuring valuations, which, though, are not at extremes, as earnings have been rising faster than prices this year. Outside of the S&P 500, most asset classes trade roughly in line with their 10-year average price-to-earnings multiple, with even many mega-cap tech names trading at a relative discount to the index.
